title: Scalable and Consistent Graph Neural Networks for Distributed Mesh-based Data-driven Modeling
problem: Enabling scalable GNN training and inference across distributed systems for mesh-based modeling while maintaining arithmetic consistency when graphs are partitioned across multiple ranks. A GNN trained on a single unified graph must produce identical results to distributed evaluations on partitioned subgraphs.
motivation: Mesh-based data-driven modeling for scientific applications like CFD requires both exascale scalability and correctness guarantees, making consistent distributed GNNs critical for production scientific computing workflows.
method: The approach develops a consistent neural message passing layer that operates on partitioned mesh graphs using halo nodes at sub-graph boundaries. GNNs are integrated with NekRS (an exascale CFD solver) where mesh partitioning directly informs distributed GNN training and inference routines. Arithmetic equivalence between single-rank and multi-rank computations is maintained through proper boundary information handling in the message passing mechanism.
key_novelty: Using consistent neural message passing with halo nodes to ensure distributed GNNs are arithmetically equivalent to centralized counterparts while scaling to billions of graph nodes.
contributions: Consistent neural message passing layer for distributed GNNs on partitioned mesh graphs
Integration methodology linking mesh partitioning to distributed GNN training and inference
Demonstration of efficient scaling to O(1B) graph nodes on Frontier exascale supercomputer
Validation of arithmetic consistency across distributed ranks
primary_theme: Consistent distributed GNNs for exascale scientific computing
